trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Tag_Processor, which the docs recommend for filling untrusted values into a fixed markup template with byte-exact output. All called APIs are documented: __construct(), next_tag(), set_attribute(), next_token(), get_token_type(), set_modifiable_text(), and get_updated_html(). Correctly preserved attribute order by predeclaring attributes in the template and used modifiable text for caption encoding. Execution passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial. The docs were effective for this task because the Tag Processor documentation contains a directly relevant 'Building markup from a template' section: it says to start with a literal template, preinclude attributes to preserve written order, include placeholder text for elements whose text will be replaced, use set_attribute() with plain unescaped strings, replace #text with set_modifiable_text(), and return get_updated_html(). The set_attribute() section also clearly explains that existing attributes keep their position while newly added attributes are sorted, which prevented the common src/alt ordering failure. The set_modifiable_text() and get_modifiable_text() sections clearly state the decoded/plaintext contract, which prevented double-escaping and prevented captions like '<script>...</script>' from being parsed as markup. Near-misses: all candidates relied on the first #text token after the img being the caption placeholder; this is correct for the compact template, but a formatted template with whitespace text nodes could mislead the same pattern. They also did not check the return value of set_modifiable_text(), despite that section saying to check it; the specific #text replacement made this harmless here.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Tag_Processor docs: 'Building markup from a template' and set_modifiable_text()
doc_gaps.problem: The template-building example demonstrates set_modifiable_text() without checking its boolean return, while the method documentation says callers should always check it. This weakens the general contract even though it did not break these trials.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Align the examples with the method contract: either check the return value in examples, or explicitly state the narrow cases where a known literal #text placeholder makes failure impossible enough to omit handling.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Tag_Processor docs: 'Building markup from a template'
doc_gaps.problem: The placeholder-text guidance does not warn that incidental formatting whitespace is also #text. A model could copy the pattern into a multi-line template and replace whitespace before the intended element instead of the actual placeholder.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note that formatted templates create whitespace text tokens, and recommend using a unique placeholder token or walking until the intended placeholder text/token is found before calling set_modifiable_text().

doc_gaps.problem: The section mostly encourages get_token_type() for '#text' checks, but one example uses get_token_name() in that role, which can blur the distinction between token type and token name.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Use get_token_type() consistently for static token-type checks such as '#text', and reserve get_token_name() examples for tag names or token-name-specific behavior.
